Q4 2025 Physics Course Schedule

Honors Physics & Standard Physics - 4 Week Schedule

Week Honors Physics (Advanced) Standard Physics
1 Unit 7: Waves and Harmonics
- Wave-Particle Duality
- Photon Energy (E = hf)
- Wave Equation (λf = c)
- Photoelectric Effect
- Energy Quantization Concepts

Lab: Photoelectric Effect Simulation		 L1 - Safe Driving Statistics
- Analysis of traffic collision data
- Pattern recognition in vehicle fatality data
- Collision modeling with paper strips
- Video analysis of real-world collisions

L2 - Distracted Driving
- P/T and V/T graphing
- Comparing motion graphs for distracted/non-distracted scenarios
- Analyzing reaction time data
2 Unit 7: Waves and Harmonics
- Electric Charges and Fields
- Coulomb’s Law (F = k(q₁q₂)/r²)
- Electric Field Strength (E = F/q)
- Gauss’s Law
- Electric Potential

Lab: Electric Field Mapping		 L3 - Speed and Collisions (avoidance)
- V-T Graphing
- Reaction Distance (d = v × t)
- Braking Distance (d = v²/(2μg))
- Total Stopping Distance calculations
- Engineering faster reaction times (HUD, Cameras)

L4 - Speed and Collision (outcomes)
- Analyzing collision data
- Force-time relationships
- Newton’s Second Law (F = ma)
- Introduction to impulse (J = F·Δt)
3 Unit 7: Waves and Harmonics
- Electromagnetic Power and Energy
- Electric Power (P = VI)
- Faraday’s Law
- Energy in Electric Fields (UE = ½CV²)
- Energy in Magnetic Fields (UB = ½LI²)

Lab: Electromagnetic Induction		 L5 - Mass, Speed, Force
- Kinetic Energy (KE = ½mv²)
- Momentum (p = mv)
- Elastic vs. inelastic collisions
- Coefficient of restitution
- Safety features analysis (crumple zones, airbags)

L6 - Lab: Momentum and Impulse Carts
- Experimental design
- Collecting collision data
- Calculating pre/post collision momentum
- Verifying conservation principles
4 Unit 9: Electricity
- Electrostatics
- Capacitance (C = Q/V)
- Electric Field (E = F/q)
- Potential Difference (V = W/q)
- Capacitor Energy (U = ½CV²)

Lab: Capacitor Charging/Discharging		 L7 - Assessment: Vehicle Stopping Times
- Comprehensive problem solving
- Multi-step collision scenarios
- Engineering design challenge
- Bus safety data analysis
- Evidence-based safety solutions

Review:
- Force (F = ma)
- Momentum (p = mv)
- Impulse (J = FΔt = Δp)
- Kinetic Energy (KE = ½mv²)
